correctness.rationale: The two-state nonrenewed Cox reset backward equations are explicitly solved by the positive-definite two-by-two matrix exponential. The exact two phase means follow by self-consistency; low and high eigenprojector expansions give the square-root slow barrier and the first fast correction. The constant-rate derivative has a unique strictly positive root. Continuity and endpoint behavior prove existence of a finite optimum for target parameter above that root. Embedded generator consistency plus independent exact-path simulations passed 739 checks; simulations do not certify infinite-parameter claims.

value.rationale: A stationary spatial resetting distribution does not determine when switching modulation improves search. The result quantifies an unavoidable inverse-square-root delay from rare entry into a resetting phase and proves a nontrivial rate-design criterion: finite environmental modulation can beat infinitely rapid self-averaging even with the same stationary mean resetting intensity. This addresses a physically motivated search/feedback parameter rather than a routine numeric slice.
